rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Carbon is the element of two worlds. **Crystalline:** diamond (sp³, 3-D tetrahedral network — hardest natural solid, thermal-conduction champion, electrical insulator, RI 2.42, for cutting tools and jewellery), graphite (sp², hexagonal layers with one delocalised electron per atom — soft, slippery, conducting along planes, for electrodes, pencils, lubricants and nuclear moderators), and C₆₀ buckminsterfullerene…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Pencil vs drill bit*** - the pencil "lead" writes because graphite layers shear off one at a time; the diamond drill bit cuts rock because its 3-D sp3 network refuses to shear in any direction.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Element That Builds Two Worlds Carbon: 4 electrons, 4 bonds, catenation without rival. Crystalline (diamond, graphite, fullerene) and amorphous (charcoal, coke, carbon black) forms; structure, general properties and uses of each.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Why carbon is special - **Catenation:** C–C bond 355 kJ/mol — strong enough for chains, rings, sheets and cages of thousands of atoms. Silicon's Si–Si (222 kJ/mol) barely chains. - **Tetravalency + hybridisation:** sp³, sp², sp give diamond, graphite and fullerene from the same atom. - Isotopes ¹²C (98.9%), ¹³C (1.1%, NMR), ¹⁴C (trace, dating, t½ 5730 y).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Diamond sp3 = hard + insulator + thermal conductor; graphite sp2 = soft + conductor + lubricant; C60 = 20 hexagons + 12 pentagons. Coke = metallurgical reducer; charcoal = adsorption. C-C 355 kJ/mol; densities 3.51 vs 2.25.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Compare diamond and graphite with respect to structure, electrical conductivity and hardness, explaining the differences.** — **Structure:** diamond is **sp³**-hybridised carbon in a 3-D tetrahedral network, every atom bonded to four neighbours by strong σ bonds (bond length 154 pm); graphite is **sp²**-hybridised…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): What is buckminsterfullerene? Describe its structure and give one use.** — **C₆₀**, discovered in 1985 (Kroto, Curl, Smalley — Nobel Prize 1996), is a football-shaped molecule about 0.7 nm across: a truncated icosahedron of **20 hexagons and 12 pentagons**, all carbons sp²-hybridised but strained at the pentagon…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For the diamond-graphite question, name the hybridisation, the bonding consequence, and one use each - three linked marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Hybridisation is destiny: sp3 locks every electron into a sigma bond (diamond - hard, insulating) while sp2 leaves one electron delocalised per atom (graphite - soft, conducting); the same element builds opposite materials by rearranging its own bonding.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Carbon: tetravalent, catenation champion (C-C 355 kJ/mol), isotopes C-12/C-13/C-14 (t1/2 5730 y). Crystalline allotropes: DIAMOND sp3 3-D tetrahedral network - hardest natural solid (10), thermal conductor, insulator, RI 2.42, density 3.51; uses cutting/jewellery/heat sinks.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A one-gram piece of good activated charcoal hides a surface area near 1000 square metres - two tennis courts folded into a sugar cube.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Why is charcoal used in gas masks and sugar refining?** — Charcoal is amorphous carbon: disordered micro-crystals of graphite riddled with pores, giving an enormous internal surface area (good activated charcoal ≈ **1000 m²/g**).…

rows.text: List the amorphous forms of carbon with one use of each.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions - **"Graphite is amorphous."** No — it is crystalline (X-ray proves sharp layers); charcoal and soot are the amorphous ones. - **"Diamond conducts electricity because it is pure carbon."** Diamond is an insulator; graphite conducts. Purity is irrelevant — hybridisation decides.…  ·  ## 7. Exam Application - The diamond-graphite contrast (hybridisation → hardness/conductivity) is the classic 3-mark question. - Quote numbers: C–C 355 kJ/mol, densities 3.51 vs 2.25, hardness 10. - Amorphous uses: tie each to adsorption or reduction.
